clue.text: Left before the church's recess — a moral slip

indicators.note: before places the abbreviation ahead of the next piece in the answer

parts.note: the apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: A churchgoer who walks out early commits a small sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a falling-off from proper conduct, a minor failing of morals or duty.

clue.text: Least suitable Shakespearean recruit's call up — that's the limit

parts.note: the last person for a job is the least suitable one

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Wart is one of the ragged men Falstaff recruits in Henry IV Part 2; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: The poorest of Falstaff's conscripts being called up is too much to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff's recruits in Henry IV Part 2 (Mouldy, Shadow, Wart, Feeble, Bullcalf) are notoriously unfit, so the poorest is the least suitable; 'call up' reads the recruit backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb about the straw that broke the camel's back: the final burden beyond what can be tolerated.

clue.text: Publicity fuss for the Spanish exhibition

parts.note: PR is short for public relations, i.e. publicity
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A promotion row erupts over a show in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is Spain's national art museum, housing a vast permanent display of paintings.

clue.text: Had cine made to show Australian burrowing egg-layer

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A nature film was shot to show an unusual Australian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea is a monotreme, one of the few mammals that lay eggs, and it digs for shelter.

clue.text: Sound profit for Carmen's producer on small royalty

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it

parts.note: Geo. is the abbreviated form of George, the name of several British kings, so a shortened royal

indicators.note: the letters of the name are worked over to produce a new arrangement

parts.note: the name of Bizet's heroine, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: An opera house's backer makes a tidy sum by staging Carmen for a minor royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound profit' is a sounds-like definition: heard as 'prophet', which a diviner is. 'producer' works over the heroine's name; Geo. is how George is abbreviated on old coins and documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A geomancer foretells the future from patterns in earth or dots, so is a kind of seer whose name is said like 'profit'.

clue.text: Disembark in, say, rising swell

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the abbreviation is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
a swell is a toff, a smartly dressed upper-class person

explanation.surface: Passengers leave the ship as the sea gets rougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EG to GE. 'swell' looks like the sea but means a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a ship, bus or train is to leave it, as passengers going ashore do.

clue.text: Set up a banking system with a union for 18

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: giro is a bank or post office system of credit transfer
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A trade union is involved in setting up a new banking system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns GIRO to ORIG. '18' is a cross-reference: the answer to 18 Down, an aromatic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The marjoram genus includes dittany of Crete, the aromatic herb at 18, so the genus name covers that plant.

clue.text: Rocky atoll harbouring unknown duck and salamander

indicators.note: harbouring means taking something in, so one piece holds the others
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of atoll are shaken up

parts.note: in algebra x is the usual unknown quantity
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so O

explanation.surface: A stony coral island shelters a mystery waterfowl and an amphibian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' rearranges ATOLL into ALOTL, and 'harbouring' puts X and O inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mexican axolotl is a salamander that keeps its gills and larval form throughout adult life.

clue.text: Barge into Alan Cabot awkwardly

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters of the names tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily bumps into a man called Alan Cabot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge into' reads as a verb, shoving into someone; 'Barge' is a noun and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowboat or barge is built to travel the canals of Britain.

clue.text: Knots sailors should not get entangled with

definitions.meaning: the square knot used for tying in sails is named after shortening sail

definitions.text: sailors should not get entangled with
definitions.meaning: rocky ridges just beneath the sea's surface that wreck ships

explanation.surface: Seamen are warned against getting tangled up in some knots.
explanation.definitionFit: The square knot sailors tie bears this name, and the word also means submerged rock or coral ridges that ships must avoid.

clue.text: Stick together past a junction of this sort

definitions.text: Stick together past a junction of this sort

parts.words: Stick together past a junction of this sort
parts.note: read 'past a' as 'pasta': strands of a long thin pasta that cling together, also the nickname of a famously tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham

explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strands of this pasta clump together, and Birmingham's Gravelly Hill motorway interchange is nicknamed after the dish.

clue.text: Wildcat in Troy

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard of Central Asia goes by this old name
troy weight, used for gold and silver, has a unit of this name

explanation.surface: A wild beast roams the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called this, and troy weight for precious metals uses a unit of the same name, twelve to the troy pound.

clue.text: It gave a sycophant a nasty hangover

definitions.text: It gave a sycophant a nasty hangover

parts.words: It gave a sycophant a nasty hangover
parts.note: not a drinking tale: the flatterer of Dionysius of Syracuse was seated beneath a blade hung by a single hair

explanation.definitionFit: Damocles, a fawning courtier, was feasted under a blade suspended by one horsehair, so a peril literally hung over him.

clue.text: Burma's revolutionary measures

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so the letters of the country's name are rearranged

parts.note: the country name with its S, used letter by letter

explanation.surface: Uprisings in Burma lead to emergency measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a Cuban dance, and 'measures' is an old word for dances or dance steps.

clue.text: Dessert wine Simon the Cellarer set some store by

definitions.meaning: a sweet wine served with pudding

definitions.text: Simon the Cellarer set some store by
definitions.meaning: the Victorian song 'Simon the Cellarer' says he keeps a rare store of Malmsey and this wine

explanation.surface: A sweet wine that a famous cellarman prized highly.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Simon the Cellarer, from a popular Victorian ballad, 'keeps a rare store of Malmsey and Malvoisie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet wine of the Malmsey family, served with dessert, and listed in the song as part of Simon's cellar stock.

clue.text: Beef not available, so have a game starter

parts.note: bully beef is canned corned beef, so bully alone can mean beef
a dish that is off is no longer on the menu

explanation.surface: With no beef on the menu, a diner settles for a game pie instead.
explanation.walkthrough: BULLY beef is British canned corned beef. A bully-off is how a hockey game used to start.
explanation.definitionFit: In hockey, play once began with two players tapping sticks before striking at the ball, which restarts or opens the match.

clue.text: Imagine Frank not in love!

parts.note: to fancy something is to imagine it
frank and free both mean open or unrestrained

explanation.surface: Picture Frank, unattached and single!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning open.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unattached, with no romantic commitment, is said to be footloose and unattached in this way.

clue.text: Iodine sister put on friend in flood

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
a nun is a religious sister
a date is a boyfriend or girlfriend

explanation.surface: A nurse applies iodine to a companion caught in a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, as a river bursting its banks swamps the land.

clue.text: Fairly roasted when spring ended

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
done means finished or ended

explanation.surface: The joint was nicely cooked by the time spring was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly' is used in its old sense of fully or thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked right through, with no pink left, is described this way; 'fairly' here means completely.

clue.text: Song about an aromatic plant

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A ballad about a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dittany of Crete is a fragrant herb of the mint family, long used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Sea-god's noisy struggle with heavyweight

indicators.note: something noisy is heard, so the word for the struggle is used for its sound

parts.note: to try is to strive or struggle
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A god of the deep wrestles loudly with a massive opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Sea-god's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton, son of Poseidon, was the Greek merman who blew a conch shell to calm or raise the waves.

clue.text: Rave about the priest being dependent

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to rant is to rave
Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A tirade about a cleric who relies on others.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel, a crossword regular for 'priest'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reliant on something is to depend on it, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Akin to a mosquito, almost the last of the species

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting fly such as a mosquito

indicators.note: the letter just before the final one, the penultimate letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gnat is nearly the last surviving insect of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost the last of the species' is the penultimate letter of 'species', E.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate means related through the male line, hence closely related or of the same kind.

clue.text: Taking pictures of the gods at short range

parts.note: photographers and film crews are said to be shooting
in a theatre, the gods are the highest balcony seats, also called the gallery

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps divine figures from close quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The gods' is theatre slang for the top tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground stall or indoor facility for target practice is a small enclosed firing range.

clue.text: The way an artist comprehends universal Hindu aphorisms

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include or take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter grasps universal wisdom from Hindu sayings.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) is the stock crossword artist, and U is the British film rating for universal audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist literature, a sutra is a collection of terse sayings or a rule-like teaching.

clue.text: Another religious book with pictures turned up

parts.note: Ex. is the abbreviation for Exodus, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: art is pictures, paintings

explanation.surface: Another illustrated Bible has surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Exodus is abbreviated Ex., so 'religious book' gives two letters; 'turned up' reads the pictures word upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional one, so it can stand for 'another' as in 'one more'.

clue.text: Opera that Oscar Wilde contributed to

indicators.note: the words named each contribute some of their letters to the answer, which is lodged inside them

explanation.surface: Wilde is said to have had a hand in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's work about a singer, her lover and the police chief Scarpia is one of the best-known operas.

clue.text: Translucent white flower on Welsh lake returning

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it
returning means the name of the lake is read backwards

parts.note: Bala Lake (Llyn Tegid) is the largest natural lake in Wales
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A pale bloom floats on a lake in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine-grained gypsum is prized for its milky translucence, and the word describes skin or stone of that pale tone.

clue.text: It makes a light, neat lycée building

indicators.note: building puts the letters together into a new structure

parts.note: a French secondary school, used here letter by letter without the accent

explanation.surface: A tidy French school building is admired.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas burns with a brilliant flame and was used in old miners' and bicycle lamps, and in welding torches.

clue.text: Article about an old chief of clan

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing concerns a Highland leader of old.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a thane was a chief of a clan or a nobleman holding land from the king, as Macbeth was.
